strings.name: Pat Gelsinger
strings.summary: Gelsinger joined Intel from technical school and earned university degrees while working, helping develop the 80486 and other computing technologies before becoming Intel's first CTO. He then worked at EMC and led VMware. Returning as Intel CEO in 2021, he pursued manufacturing and foundry expansion, but the turnaround fell short and he left in 2024. He later joined Playground Global and took leadership roles at Gloo and xLight.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: His Intel engineering and VMware leadership influenced processor design, virtualization and semiconductor manufacturing strategy.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Associate degree, Lincoln Technical Institute; bachelor's, Santa Clara (1983); master's, Stanford (1985).
strings.highlights.h1.title: From chip engineering to leadership
strings.highlights.h1.text: As 80486 architect and Intel's first CTO, he linked processor design with industry technologies and standards.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Hardware and cloud software
strings.highlights.h2.text: After leading enterprise infrastructure and VMware, he moved into early-stage technology investment.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Joining Playground Global
strings.timeline.t1.text: He became a general partner and executive chairman of xLight, which develops free-electron-laser light sources.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Expanded Gloo role
strings.timeline.t2.text: He moved from investment and board work to executive chair and head of technology for products serving faith organizations.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Leaving Intel
strings.timeline.t3.text: He left the CEO and board roles as manufacturing transformation and operating pressures prompted a succession process.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Returning as Intel CEO
strings.timeline.t4.text: He left VMware to pursue a manufacturing revival and external foundry services.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Leading VMware
strings.timeline.t5.text: He led the virtualization and cloud-infrastructure company until 2021.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joining EMC
strings.timeline.t6.text: He became president and COO of information infrastructure products, covering storage and enterprise technology.
strings.timeline.t7.title: 80486 introduced
strings.timeline.t7.text: He served as architect of the processor and helped develop Intel's microprocessor business.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Entering Intel
strings.timeline.t8.text: After technical school, he began engineering work and continued university education alongside it.
